newsItems.headline: Jim Cramer sees more upside for Goldman and addresses Wells Fargo's biggest question
Buffett says Trump's pick of Kevin Warsh for Fed chair was 'good choice'

briefing.briefing: Right now, gold is being supported by a combination of falling bond yields [the interest rate the US government pays to borrow money — when yields fall, gold becomes more attractive because it has no yield to compare against], a softer US Dollar [DXY at 100.48, which is relatively weak], and elevated geopolitical risk [the GPR index sits at 173.6, meaning global tension is above normal, which traditionally pushes money into gold as a 'safe haven']. The 10-year real yield [the return on US bonds after stripping out inflation — the most important competitor to gold] dropped 3 basis points overnight and sits at 2.33%, a modest tailwind for gold. On recent news, there is honestly nothing market-moving to flag in the last few hours — a Jim Cramer banking comment from 16.5 hours ago and a Warren Buffett quote about a potential future Fed Chair nominee (Kevin Warsh) from nearly 20 hours ago are the only headlines available, and neither directly drives a dollar or gold move today. The directional bias leans mildly BULLISH — gold at $4,029 is in record territory, yields are easing slightly, the dollar is soft, and speculative positioning [large traders are net-long 183,165 contracts, meaning the crowd is betting on higher prices] remains constructive. However, ETF flows [money moving in or out of gold funds] are flat for three straight weeks, which suggests big institutional buyers are not adding aggressively right now, capping conviction. Confidence is 5/10 — the trend is up but momentum evidence is thin this morning and we are in the quieter Asian session. What would change this view: a sharp Dollar rally or a spike in US yields would flip the bias bearish quickly. There are NO calendar events showing for today, which is unusual — an empty calendar can mean a quieter, choppier session, but also means no scheduled landmines to dodge. No high-impact events are flagged for later this week in the data either, so there is no specific build-up caution needed beyond normal awareness. On key levels: the 14-day Average Daily Range [the typical distance gold travels in a day] is 98.3 points, and price has already used 42.5 of those points today, meaning roughly 55 points of typical daily movement may remain — watch for potential resistance near $4,055–4,060 and support back around $3,987–4,000. For trade integration: this is the Asian session, which is typically the quietest and least reliable for ICT-style trend trades — wait for the London open (8:00 AM GMT) to see if price forms a clear higher-low structure on the 1H chart before committing; keep position size small given moderate confidence, and only buy pullbacks into structure, not breakouts into thin air. If the trend is your friend, patience is your best trade management tool.
